note: What a charm is said to be for, in the words the tradition uses. This project reports the claim and names who makes it. It does not test the claim and does not rank charms by it.

entries.label: The evil eye
entries.gloss: harm carried by a look, often an admiring one

entries.label: Envy
entries.gloss: a neighbour's ill will, named as such

entries.label: Illness
entries.gloss: sickness in general, where no cause is named

entries.label: Harm to a child
entries.gloss: harm to an infant or a small child; common across the atlas, though not the largest class in it — see /story/most-of-them-are-for-children/

entries.label: A road accident
entries.gloss: the modern descendant of the travel charm

entries.label: A court case or an official
Failing an exam
entries.gloss: a whole modern genre, Japan and Korea especially

entries.label: Danger to the dead
entries.gloss: charms put in a grave for the person in it

entries.label: Harm to a house or a field
Attracting custom, luck or love
entries.gloss: the charm that pulls rather than blocks
